questions.q: What are the three decisions every report in Report Designer requires, in order?
options: A data source (table), a report type, and a group-by field
A chart color, a title, and a legend position
A user role, a schedule, and an email list
A dashboard, a tab, and a widget size
questions.explain: Report Designer builds every report from a table, a report type, and a field to group by — skip any one and there's nothing to chart.

questions.q: Which real out-of-box report type cross-tabulates two fields at once, with an aggregation in each cell?
options: Time Series
List
Pivot Table
Pie chart
questions.explain: A Pivot Table puts one field down the rows and another across the columns, with a count or sum where they intersect — for example priority by assignment group.

questions.q: A Service Desk Manager wants to know the average time-to-resolve per assignment group. What aggregation does the report need?
options: Count
Average
Sum
No aggregation is needed
questions.explain: Count tells you how many records are in a group; average time-to-resolve requires the average aggregation on a numeric duration field.

questions.q: Why does a 'Pie chart of open incidents by priority' need a filter condition in addition to a group-by field?
options: Filters are optional cosmetic settings with no effect on the data
Without a filter, the chart includes every incident ever created, open or closed, not just the open ones
Pie charts cannot use filters, only Bar charts can
The group-by field already excludes closed incidents automatically
questions.explain: The group-by field only controls how records are split into slices; an Active/State filter is what limits the report to open incidents in the first place.

questions.q: How can a report reach a manager's inbox automatically without them logging into ServiceNow?
options: Reports cannot be delivered outside the platform
By scheduling the report to run and email itself on a recurring basis
By converting it to a Performance Analytics widget
By exporting it manually to a shared drive every week
questions.explain: A scheduled report runs automatically on a recurrence (daily, weekly, monthly, or custom) and emails itself to chosen users or groups.
